llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed model-pricing and recommendation integration that makes purpose-aligned external API calls without evidence of hidden persistence, destructive behavior, or unrelated data access.

dimensions.detail: Network calls to InferenceIndexer are disclosed and proportionate for current pricing data; the DeepInfra URL appears as an example provider endpoint rather than hidden exfiltration.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill declares an inferenceindexer MCP server requirement and references a PyPI MCP server and auto-discovery URL, but it does not include installer code or hidden setup actions.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation language is broad around model choice and cost concerns, so users should expect it to run during model-selection discussions; the behavior remains tied to pricing and recommendation tasks.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No local persistence, privilege escalation, scheduled tasks, tool wrapping, or memory writes were found; the anonymous key section notes third-party usage history for that service.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to recommend and price-check AI models, and the MCP tools plus bundled cost-audit script are aligned with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this if you are comfortable sending model-selection constraints, model IDs, and related pricing questions to InferenceIndexer. Avoid letting it inspect sensitive usage logs unless you explicitly want a cost audit, and review any recommended provider switch before changing production traffic.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The skill uses an MCP server and external pricing API because its purpose is live model recommendation; lack of a tighter declared tool scope is a disclosure/least-privilege note, not evidence of hidden behavior.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger language can cause frequent activation during model-selection or cost conversations, but those scenarios match the skill's stated purpose.
[E1] expected: The DeepInfra URL is shown in a sample endpoint_config returned as a model-hosting recommendation, not as bundled code that sends user data there.
[E1] expected: The InferenceIndexer API and anonymous-key endpoint are disclosed integration points for pricing data access; users should understand this creates a third-party dependency.
